title: Dating Benefit Payments in the Waiver Income Window — Benefit Overpayment Accounts Interpretive Note
content:
When the countable annual income on a Benefit Overpayment Accounts waiver request is worked out, the dating of the claimant's benefit payments follows what the income window contains. The income window is the three whole months before the handling date: an entry falls in it when the whole months from its date to the handling date are fewer than 3. The payments and cancellations are those on the ledgers of the claimant's Unemployment Benefit Claims.

| What the income window contains | How the benefit payments are counted |
|---|---|
| A supplemental payment issued in the income window | Every payment is counted by the week it pays for rather than by its issue date, so back pay for weeks ending before the window drops out |
| No supplemental payment, but a cancelled payment falls in the window | Payments are counted by issue date, less the payments cancelled in the window |
| Otherwise | Payments are counted by issue date |

## Interpretation

- A supplemental payment is a benefit payment whose kind on the claim ledger is supplemental. Its issue date decides whether it is in the window.
- Counting "by the week it pays for" means that a payment is taken when the week ending date of the week it pays for falls in the window, whatever its issue date.
- A cancelled payment falls in the window when the cancellation entry on the claim ledger is dated in the window; the amounts of those cancellation entries are what is subtracted.

## Hypothetical case

Handling date 20 June. A supplemental payment of USD 450.00 was issued on 5 May for the week ending 8 March, and weekly payments for weeks ending 28 March to 13 June were issued during the window.

- The supplemental payment is in the window, so every payment is counted by the week it pays for.
- The week ending 8 March is three whole months before 20 June and falls outside: the USD 450.00 of back pay drops out.
- The weekly payments for weeks ending 28 March to 13 June are counted.
